title: Myeloproliferative neoplasms: polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, and myelofibrosis

units.name: Introduction
units.assessment: Can you name the three driver mutations of the classical MPNs, say roughly what fraction of PV, ET and myelofibrosis carries each, and explain how they converge on the same signaling pathway?

lesson.title: Stefan Constantinescu: MOLECULAR PATHOGENESIS OF HUMAN MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS
lesson.why: A molecular-pathogenesis lecture from one of the laboratories that worked out JAK2 and CALR signaling — why three different mutations produce one activated pathway and three phenotypes.

units.assessment: Can you list the current diagnostic criteria for polycythemia vera, say what the erythropoietin level and marrow biopsy add, and explain how masked PV differs from a secondary erythrocytosis?

units.assessment: Can you state the hematocrit target for a patient with PV, say who needs cytoreduction rather than phlebotomy and aspirin alone, and name the options when hydroxyurea fails or is not tolerated?

lesson.why: A How I Treat summary from an author of the PV risk classification: hematocrit target, aspirin, who gets cytoreduced and what follows hydroxyurea failure.
